sentences.sentence: Generic name: meloxicam (oral/injection) [ mel-OKS-i-kam ] Brand names: Anjeso , Mobic , Qamzova , Xifyrm , Vivlodex , Qmiiz ODT Dosage form: intravenous dispersion (30 mg/mL), oral capsule (10 mg; 5 mg), oral suspension (7.5 mg/5 mL), oral tablet (15 mg; 7.5 mg), single-dose vial for intravenous injection (30 mg/1 mL) Drug class: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatories (NSAIDs)
Medically reviewed by Philip Thornton, DipPharm .
Last updated on Aug 13, 2026.
Meloxicam is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID).
It works by reducing hormones that cause pain, fever, and inflammation in the body.

Meloxicam is used to relieve pain, tenderness, swelling, and stiffness caused by osteoarthritis (arthritis caused by a breakdown of the lining of the joints) and rheumatoid arthritis (arthritis caused by swelling of the lining of the joints).

Meloxicam is also used to relieve the pain, tenderness, swelling, and stiffness caused by juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (a type of arthritis that affects children) in children 2 years of age and older.
IV meloxicam (brands Anjeso [discontinued], Qamzova, Xifyrm) is used for moderate to severe pain in adults, alone or in combination with non-NSAID analgesics.
Vivlodex capsules [discontinued] are only for use in adults.
Qmiiz ODT (orally disintegrating tablet) [discontinued] is for adults and children weighing at least 132 pounds (60 kilograms).
Generic meloxicam is available.
Meloxicam can increase your risk of a fatal heart attack or stroke, especially if you use it long term or take high doses, or if you have heart disease.
Even people without heart disease or risk factors could have a stroke or heart attack while taking this medicine.
Do not use this medicine just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Avoid taking meloxicam after a recent heart attack, unless your doctor tells you to.
You may have an increased risk of another heart attack if you take this medicine after a recent heart attack.
Get emergency medical help if you have chest pain, weakness, shortness of breath, slurred speech, or problems with vision or balance.
Meloxicam may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding, which can be fatal.
These conditions can occur without warning while you are using this medicine, especially in older adults.
Call your doctor at once if you have symptoms of stomach bleeding, such as black, bloody, or tarry stools, or coughing up blood or vomit that looks like coffee grounds.
Avoid smoking and drinking alcohol, as they also increase your risk of stomach bleeding.

Meloxicam is not approved for use by anyone younger than 2 years old.
If you are pregnant, you should not take meloxicam unless your doctor tells you to.
Taking an NSAID at about 20 weeks of pregnancy or later may harm your unborn baby.
If you need to take this medicine for more than 2 days when you are between 20 and 30 weeks of pregnancy, your doctor may need to monitor the amount of fluid around your baby.
You should not take meloxicam after about 30 weeks of pregnancy.
Meloxicam may cause a delay in ovulation (the release of an egg from an ovary).
You should not take this medicine if you are undergoing fertility treatment or are otherwise trying to get pregnant.
Ask a doctor if it is safe to breastfeed while using this medicine.
Take Meloxicam exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Use the lowest effective dose for your condition.
Meloxicam oral is taken by mouth.
Meloxicam injection (Qamzova, Xifyrm) is given as an intravenous bolus injection over 15 seconds.
A healthcare provider will give you this injection.
Your dose needs may change if you switch to a different brand, strength, or form of meloxicam.
Avoid medication errors by using only the medicine your doctor prescribes.
Meloxicam doses are based on weight (especially in children and teenagers).
Your dose needs may change if you gain or lose weight.
If you use this medicine long-term, you may need frequent medical tests.
Store oral suspension, tablets, or capsules at room temperature, away from moisture and heat.
Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use.

Meloxicam is stronger, prescription-only, longer-acting, and used mainly for arthritis; ibuprofen is milder, OTC, shorter-acting, and treats various pains.
Meloxicam can be taken in the morning or at night.
Oral meloxicam is usually taken once daily, at about the same time each day.
You can take it with or without food, but food may help with stomach upset.
Follow your prescribed dose and do not take more than recommended.

Meloxicam usually starts to ease pain within the first day, but the full benefit for chronic conditions like osteoarthritis can take several days to a couple of weeks.
How quickly you feel relief depends on the dose, the formulation (oral tablet vs intravenous), and whether you are treating short‑term postoperative pain or long‑term arthritis.

The amount of meloxicam you can give your dog will depend on your dog’s weight and veterinarian’s instructions.
The typical dose is 0.09 mg/lb (0.2 mg/kg) on day 1 given by mouth or mixed with food, then 0.045 mg/lb (0.1 mg/kg) once a day.
If you are switching from ibuprofen to meloxicam, wait until the ibuprofen has worn off before taking your first dose of meloxicam.
For most people, that’s about 6 hours after the last dose of ibuprofen.
Both meloxicam and Celebrex are prescription NSAIDs that treat arthritis pain and swelling, and for most people they work about the same.
Celebrex is a more “stomach‑friendly” COX‑2 selective drug while meloxicam usually costs less and lasts longer in the body.
